located_point.method: Centre of the rectangular water-filled basin (the dock) on the Sentinel-2 median composite, inside the vegetated oval mound about 170 m north of the Wikidata starting point (22.521389, 72.249444); the excavated, bright acropolis area lies immediately west of the basin and the museum buildings south of the mound, matching the site plan's layout of dock, platform and acropolis.

notes: Imagery resolves one Harappan feature, the dock: both long edges of its water-filled basin were fitted on B08. The rest of the excavated area is visible only as irregular bright patches that cannot be tied to particular walls at 10 m. The plan sources disagree with each other: the schematic site plan (plan-lothal-01) draws the dock as a skewed parallelogram turned about 5.5 degrees clockwise from its arrow, the warehouse plan (Fig. 18) gives block faces within a few degrees of its arrow, and the B-block plan (Fig. 17) gives house walls about 10 degrees anticlockwise of its arrow, while its dash-dot excavation grid is drawn square to the page and 18.7 degrees from the arrow. None of the arrows states its meaning. In plan-lothal-01 the 'Site Boundary' lines were not measured because the plan does not identify them as a wall. In plan-rao1979-fig18 the south face of block 41h (theta 4.37) was put in its own system so that the remaining twelve block faces meet the 6 degree window; in plan-rao1979-fig17 the thin passage wall (theta -5.02, under half of its profiles inliers) was separated for the same reason. No registration was made: the only features common to imagery and plan are the dock corners, a 40 by 210 m rectangle whose ends are blurred at 10 m, so a registration would repeat the dock-line comparison with a larger error. Rao 1979 Fig. 15 (smithy and Street 1, printed page 99) and Fig. 16 (public drain) also carry arrows and were not measured.
